#SciOTD 𝗦𝗨𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗧𝗬𝗣𝗛𝗢𝗢𝗡 𝗢𝗠𝗣𝗢𝗡𝗚 (𝟮𝟬𝟭𝟴) 🌀 

On this day in 2018, Super Typhoon #OmpongPH (#Mangkhut) tore across Northern Luzon, unleashing devastation on an unprecedented scale. It left a trail of destruction worth nearly ₱34 billion and claimed 79 lives, many of which were from the massive landslide in Benguet. 

At around 1:40 AM (PHT) on September 15, Super Typhoon Ompong made landfall in Baggao, Cagayan, unleashing its fury across the provinces of Cagayan, Apayao, and Ilocos Norte before exiting into the West Philippine Sea by midday. That day, PAGASA recorded peak wind gusts of over 175 km/h in Aparri, Cagayan.

Ompong’s destructive winds ravaged communities—toppling power and communication lines, uprooting trees, and tearing through buildings, with Cagayan bearing the brunt of the impact. Torrential rains, intensified by the southwest monsoon (habagat), inundated much of Luzon, including Metro Manila and Baguio City. The deluge also triggered a deadly landslide in Itogon, Benguet, claiming dozens of lives.

According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC), Ompong left at least 79 people dead, affected 3 million residents, and caused ₱33.93 billion in damages—cementing its place as one of the most devastating cyclones in Philippine history.

“RAIN READY CARAVAN: HANDA SA ULAN, HANDA SA BAHA”
The DOST-PAGASA, through the National Capital Region-PAGASA Regional Services Division (NCR-PRSD) in partnership with the Office of Civil Defense (OCD), will conduct an online Rainfall Warning System Caravan dubbed as “Rain Ready Caravan: Handa sa Ulan, Handa sa Baha” in Central Luzon (Region III), CALABARZON (Region IV-A), and Metro Manila (National Capital Region).
The said caravan aims to (1) strengthen DRRM and LGU capacity on Rainfall Warnings and hazards of heavy rainfall, (2) promote clarity between Weather Advisories and Rainfall Warnings for disaster preparedness, (3) introduce and promote Impact-Based Forecasting, and (4) gather feedback from local early warning services for improvements.
We are enjoining all DRRM practitioners in various institutions, both public and private, as well as the Local Government Units (LGUs), academe (teachers) in Metro Manila (National Capital Region).
Let us all learn, interact, and collectively respond to the hazards of heavy rainfall! Please register in advance to receive Zoom link.

A Day of Chaos for a Night of Magic 💜

I swear the universe tested me in every way just to meet Sohee 🥺😔

Hmm..I will not say that I am a person with bad luck but I am truly a person with no luck! I’m sharing my experience and challenges to get to the 2025 HAN SOHEE 1ST FANMEETING WORLD TOUR [Xohee Loved Ones,] in MANILA.

I’ve always been busy but suddenly this became the busiest month where I worked non-stop. I only slept 2 - 3 hours each day and packed my luggage very last minute. On the 13th, I slept at 1.30AM, planned to wake at 3:30AM but only opened my eyes at 4.30AM! 😣 Rushed to the train and at 5.15AM while sitting inside I saw a notification that my 8.10AM flight was delayed to 10.25AM. That means I would only arrive in Manila at 2.30PM 🤯

At the Manila airport my e-travel form was not filled, my e-sim did not work and the wifi kept cutting off. I ended up buying a physical sim. I got stuck for 1 hour 30 minutes at the airport because of all these. Ohh and 3 immigration officers even questioned me about Sohee 😭 One of them was her fan and asked about her dramas, her latest project and the famous drama. She even hinted action and the answer is of course My Name 😅

Btw, I had actually DM’d the organiser much earlier asking if there would be any ticket counter open at the event. They told me no, tickets must be redeemed at the SM ticket outlet and it cannot be done by another person. So of course I rushed there first.

At 3.38PM I booked Grab to SM Mall to redeem my ticket. I reached there at 4.25PM but none of the guards knew the right place. They kept sending me back and forth between two different buildings. I walked around with my luggage for almost 1 hour until my moots at Okada told me the counter was open there. All that time wasted 😭😣😩😔

Traffic was terrible. I was dizzy, exhausted and almost threw up from stress. I reached the hotel at 5.46PM, queued for check in, got into the room at 6.15PM, quickly ran to the bathroom, and left again at 6.27PM. I arrived at Okada by 6.31PM. My moots helped queue for me and guided me to the right place so I could calm down a bit 🥺

I went to redeem my ticket, then headed to the gift counter. The staff took care of everything really well, even asked permission to take a picture of me holding my gifts, and I had to write my name on a paper which I can see only three fans including me sent gifts for Sohee 💜

Then I went to buy merch. The staff checked each lightstick in front of me since I was buying for others Malaysian moots too. I also bought a diary and got a pink pen ☺️ Then a familiar face appeared, the bodyguard who was with Sohee at Cannes and Dior HK. He was so kind and gave me a signed poster. Later at dinner I checked the diary and saw it was signed by Sohee too 😭🥹🩷

In the end with all the hellish chaos, I entered the event at 6.59PM when Sohee also came up to the stage!!!!😭😭😭 

but helpppp!!!! 
the adventure was not finished yet…..

+

MAPAYAPANG PAGTITIPON PATUNAY NG MATATAG NA DEMOKRASYA—PNP

Mapayapa at maayos ang mga naganap na kilos-protesta sa iba’t ibang bahagi ng Metro Manila ngayong linggo. Ayon sa Philippine National Police (PNP), ito ay bunga ng pagtutulungan ng publiko at ng kapulisan, alinsunod sa direktiba ni Pangulo Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.

Mahigit 2,100 pulis ang na-deploy at may 1,500 Reactionary Standby Support Force(RSSF) na nakaantabay upang masiguro ang kaligtasan at maayos na daloy ng trapiko. Nanatiling mahinahon at ipinamalas ang maximum tolerance ng ating kapulisan para mapakinggan ang boses ng mga nagprotesta habang napapanatili ang kaayusan.

Isinagawa ang mga pagtitipon sa mga lugar gaya ng EDSA Shrine, Ortigas (Mandaluyong–Quezon City) at iba pang pangunahing kalsada sa Metro Manila.

Ayon kay Acting Chief PNP PLTGEN Jose Melencio C. Nartatez Jr.:

“Buong puso kong pinasasalamatan ang bawat pulis na nagbantay at nagpakita ng kanilang propesyonalismo at malasakit. Ang ipinakita ninyong disiplina at paggalang sa karapatang pantao ay tunay na kahanga-hanga.”

Dagdag pa niya:

“Maraming salamat din sa mga dumalo sa rally—mga organizer at lahat ng nakiisa—sa inyong pakikipagtulungan at pagsunod sa mga patakaran. Napatunayan nating posible ang isang mapayapang pagtitipon sa isang demokrasya.”

Nanawagan ang PNP na ipagpatuloy ang ganitong kooperasyon upang manatiling ligtas at maayos ang mga susunod na pagtitipon.

Source: PNP-PIO

IN PHOTOS | Members of PUSO ng NAIA (Pagkakaisa ng User, Stakeholder, at Obrero ng NAIA) staged a die-in protest at NAIA Terminal 3 in Pasay City on September 15, 2025, to oppose rising fees and the privatization of airport operations. The group warned that unchecked increases and the handover of key functions to private interests could erode jobs, raise travel costs, and weaken NAIA’s role as the country’s primary gateway. They urged the suspension of airport fee hikes, genuine stakeholder consultations, and an independent review of the NAIA–SMC deal to protect public interest. 

📸: Norman Cruz

"I WANT TO HOLD THESE PEOPLE ACCOUNTABLE... SO I DON'T BLAME THEM'

Acknowledging public outrage over the flood-control corruption scandal, Pres. Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said that if he weren’t president, he would be out on the streets joining protests against corruption.

"Express it, you come, make your feelings known to these people and make them answerable for that wrongdoing that they have done. Ipaalam ninyo ang sentimyento, ipaalam ninyo kung paano nila kayo sinaktan, kung papaano kayo ninanakawan nitong mga ito," Marcos said, while urging demonstrators to keep the protests peaceful.

data.raw_text:
“RAIN READY CARAVAN: HANDA SA ULAN, HANDA SA BAHA”
The DOST-PAGASA, through the National Capital Region-PAGASA Regional Services Division (NCR-PRSD) in partnership with the Office of Civil Defense (OCD), will conduct an online Rainfall Warning System Caravan dubbed as “Rain Ready Caravan: Handa sa Ulan, Handa sa Baha” in Central Luzon (Region III), CALABARZON (Region IVA), and Metro Manila (National Capital Region).
The said caravan aims to (1) strengthen DRRM and LGU capacity on Rainfall Warnings and hazards of heavy rainfall, (2) promote clarity between Weather Advisories and Rainfall Warnings for disaster preparedness, (3) introduce and promote Impact-Based Forecasting, and (4) gather feedback from local early warning services for improvements.
We are enjoining all DRRM practitioners in various institutions, both public and private, as well as the Local Government Units (LGUs) in the three identified regions, to participate in the said caravan.
Let us all learn, interact, and collectively respond to the hazards of heavy rainfall! Please take a look at the post below for the schedule of activities.
